主要内容: The article discusses the concept of 'Peak Car,' highlighting the declining popularity of personal car ownership in urban areas. Larry Kim, a Boston tech executive, abandoned his Infiniti luxury sedan in 2014 and began using ride-hailing services like Uber and Lyft, spending up to $20,000 annually. He argues that the time saved by not driving is worth the cost. The article notes that auto sales in the U.S. are declining after four record or near-record years, and analysts predict they may never reach those levels again. Globally, residents are moving to megacities, where owning a car can be an expensive inconvenience. Young people are also turning away from cars, with only 26% of U.S. 16-year-olds earning a driver’s license in 2017, compared to nearly half in the 1980s. In the U.K., the number of 17-year-olds taking driving tests has dropped by 28% over the past decade.
